summary: Media queries live in CSS, but the HTML must include the viewport meta tag or phones will pretend to be a wide desktop screen and ignore your phone layout.
notes: <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> tells phones to use their real width.
The preview is about 640px wide, so it shows the tablet line and two columns.
The three .size lines are only there to show which layout is active. A real site would not need them.
pitfall: Leaving out the viewport meta tag. On a phone the page then shows as a tiny zoomed-out desktop layout.
